name: Direct Line Group
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: UK general insurer selling motor, home and other cover directly, with brands including Direct Line, Churchill and Green Flag.
capacity_detail: Aviva agreed in Dec 2024 to acquire Direct Line at a valuation of GBP 3.70bn; completed 1 July 2025
markets: United Kingdom consumers for motor, home, roadside assistance (Green Flag) and other general insurance products.
rationale: Mass-market UK consumer insurance brand with heavy advertising spend; F1's large British audience fits motor insurance and Green Flag roadside cover.

name: esure
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Internet and telephone insurer offering motor, home and travel insurance to UK consumers, including the First Alternative sub-brand.
ownership: subsidiary of Ageas (bought from Bain Capital)
capacity_detail: Bain Capital agreed in April 2025 to sell esure to Ageas for EUR 1.510bn; completed 30 September 2025
markets: United Kingdom consumers buying car, home and travel insurance online and by phone; offices in Reigate, Manchester and Glasgow.
rationale: Digital motor insurer targeting UK drivers; F1 audience overlaps with car-owning customers it acquires through brand marketing.

name: Discover Financial Services
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
industry: credit card issuer and payments network
desc: US credit card issuer and payments network operator best known for the Discover Card, now owned by Capital One.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Capital One in an all-stock deal worth about USD 35.3bn, closed 18 May 2025
markets: United States card customers; Discover/Diners Club network acceptance used by merchants and partner issuers worldwide.
rationale: Card network brand competing with Visa, Mastercard and American Express, all of which already use F1 to drive card acceptance and spend.

name: U.S. Steel
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: American integrated steelmaker producing flat-rolled and tubular steel products, now owned by Japan's Nippon Steel.
ownership: subsidiary of Nippon Steel (via Nippon Steel North America); US government holds a golden share
capacity_detail: Acquired by Nippon Steel for USD 14.9bn, closed 18 June 2025; revenue USD 15.6bn in 2024
markets: United States steel customers in automotive, construction, energy and appliances; also operations in Slovakia.
rationale: Iconic American industrial brand relaunched under Nippon Steel; US F1 growth offers automotive-customer hospitality and brand renewal.

name: Stelco
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Canadian steelmaker producing flat-rolled steel at Hamilton and Lake Erie works, acquired by Cleveland-Cliffs in 2024.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Cleveland-Cliffs for about USD 2.5bn, completed November 2024
markets: Canadian and North American steel buyers in construction, automotive and manufacturing sectors.
rationale: Steel supplier to North American automotive industry; Canadian Grand Prix hospitality could support customer relationships, though consumer pull is limited.

name: NinjaTrader
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Futures trading software, clearing and brokerage company offering desktop, web and mobile platforms for live and simulated trading.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Kraken for USD 1.5bn on 2 May 2025
markets: Retail futures traders mainly in the United States, with platform users internationally.
rationale: Retail trading brand whose rivals (eToro, Pepperstone, IC Markets) use F1 to reach affluent male traders; sister brand Kraken already sponsors Williams.

name: Toyota Industries
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Japanese manufacturer of forklifts and materials handling systems, automotive engines and compressors, logistics solutions and textile machinery.
ownership: subsidiary of Toyota Fudosan (owned by Toyota Motor 19.46%, Toyota Industries 19.43%, DENSO 19.00%, AISIN 11.00%); delisted June 2026
capacity_detail: Taken private by Toyota Fudosan via tender offer at JPY 20,600 per share, settled March 2026; Toyota Motor's stake alone priced at about JPY 1.15tn
markets: Worldwide materials handling (Raymond, Bastian Solutions), automotive components for Toyota, and textile machinery customers.
rationale: World's largest forklift group with global B2B brands; Toyota Gazoo Racing's Haas tie-up offers a ready route into F1 hospitality.

name: Preqin
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Investment data company providing data, research and analytics on private equity, private debt, real estate and other alternative assets.
capacity_detail: BlackRock agreed in July 2024 to buy Preqin for GBP 2.55bn; completion announced March 2025
markets: Investors, fund managers and advisers worldwide researching alternative assets and private markets.
rationale: B2B data brand selling to fund managers and allocators; F1 hospitality suits client entertainment, though BlackRock may fold it into Aladdin.

name: Amedisys
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: US provider of home health, hospice and high-acuity care at home, caring for about 499,000 people a year.
capacity_detail: Optum agreed in June 2023 to buy Amedisys for USD 3.3bn; acquisition completed during 2025
markets: United States patients needing home health, hospice and palliative care, referred by hospitals and physicians.
rationale: Domestic home-care brand with limited consumer marketing; US race weekends could support clinician recruitment, but F1 fit is weak.

name: Sundyne
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Designs, manufactures and services centrifugal pumps and compressors for energy, chemical, petrochemical and industrial process markets.
capacity_detail: Honeywell completed its purchase of Sundyne for USD 2.16bn, announced June 2025
markets: Oil and gas, refining, chemicals, hydrogen, renewable fuels, power generation, mining and data centre customers worldwide.
rationale: Precision-engineered pumps and compressors sold to global energy majors; F1 engineering imagery and hospitality could support B2B selling.

name: ILC Dover
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Maker of engineered flexible-material products for life sciences, aerospace and protection, best known for NASA space suits.
ownership: subsidiary of Ingersoll Rand (bought from New Mountain Capital)
capacity_detail: Ingersoll Rand closed its acquisition of ILC Dover on 3 June 2024 for about USD 2.325bn upfront in cash
markets: Biopharma, pharma, cell and gene therapy manufacturers, aerospace and space agencies, and personal protection customers.
rationale: Space-suit heritage gives a strong engineering story, but its B2B life-science buyers make F1 sponsorship a stretch.

name: Silvus Technologies
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Maker of mobile ad-hoc network radios forming self-healing mesh networks for drones, defence, public safety and enterprises.
capacity_detail: Motorola Solutions completed its acquisition of Silvus on 6 August 2025 for USD 4.4bn upfront plus up to USD 600M earnout
markets: Defence agencies, intelligence community, law enforcement, unmanned systems makers and enterprises worldwide.
rationale: Wireless mesh networking for real-time video and data echoes F1 trackside telemetry; a technical partnership could showcase reliability, though buyers are defence-led.

name: Deribit
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Cryptocurrency derivatives exchange offering options and futures on Bitcoin, Ether, Solana and other digital assets.
capacity_detail: Coinbase completed its acquisition of Deribit in August 2025 for about USD 2.9bn (USD 700M cash plus 11M Coinbase shares)
markets: Institutional and professional crypto derivatives traders worldwide, excluding restricted jurisdictions; about USD 59bn open interest in 2025.
rationale: Crypto trading brands (OKX, Kraken, Crypto.com, Coinbase) crowd F1; Deribit could use it to reach high-net-worth traders outside the US.
parent_f1: current F1 partner (Aston Martin) as Coinbase

name: Fastweb
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Italian broadband and mobile operator trading as Fastweb + Vodafone after absorbing Vodafone Italia, with the ho. mobile brand.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.809bn in 2024; Swisscom bought Vodafone Italia for EUR 8bn via Fastweb, completed 31 Dec 2024
markets: Italian consumers and businesses buying fixed broadband, mobile and enterprise connectivity services.
rationale: Merged Fastweb + Vodafone brand needs national awareness in Italy, where F1 and Ferrari have huge audiences; Monza and Imola suit activations.

name: SimCorp
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Danish provider of front-to-back investment management software and services for asset managers, pension funds and insurers.
capacity_detail: Deutsche Börse agreed in 2023 to buy SimCorp for EUR 3.9bn and announced completion on 9 November 2023
markets: Asset managers, pension funds, insurers and banks across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise software sold to institutional investors; F1 hospitality suits relationship selling, as rivals in fintech software already use F1.

name: Avangrid
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: US energy company owning regulated electric and gas utilities in New York and New England plus renewable generation.
ownership: subsidiary of Iberdrola (wholly owned since December 2024)
capacity_detail: Iberdrola paid about USD 2.55bn for the 18.4% of Avangrid it did not own, closing December 2024
markets: Electricity and gas customers in New York, Connecticut, Maine and Massachusetts, plus US renewable power buyers.
rationale: Regulated US utility with limited brand-led marketing; F1 fit is weak beyond energy-transition messaging at US races.

name: GKN Automotive
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Maker of driveline components, all-wheel-drive and eDrive systems for carmakers, with 47 plants across 19 countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Dauch Corporation (formerly American Axle), which acquired parent Dowlais Group
capacity_detail: American Axle (now Dauch) completed acquisition of GKN Automotive's parent Dowlais on 3 Feb 2026 after a USD 1.4bn offer; Dowlais revenue GBP 4.337bn in 2024
markets: Global carmakers in Europe, the Americas and Asia buying sideshafts, propshafts, AWD and electric drive systems.
rationale: Automotive engineering supplier to carmakers already in F1; eDrive and torque-vectoring technology suits technical partnership storytelling and OEM hospitality.

name: Pismo
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
industry: cloud core banking and card processing
desc: Cloud-native API platform for card issuing, core banking, digital wallets and lending used by banks, retailers and neobanks.
capacity_detail: Visa completed its acquisition of Pismo for USD 1bn in cash, announced 16 January 2024
markets: Banks, retailers and neobanks in Latin America, Asia-Pacific and Europe; clients include Citi, Itau and BTG Pactual.
rationale: B2B banking-technology brand; parent Visa already sponsors Red Bull Racing, offering a ready route to bank-client hospitality at Grands Prix.
parent_f1: current F1 partner (Red Bull Racing) as Visa

name: Olink
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Provider of high-throughput multiplex protein biomarker assays, instruments and analysis services for life-science research and drug discovery.
ownership: subsidiary of Thermo Fisher Scientific (Life Sciences Solutions segment)
capacity_detail: Thermo Fisher completed its acquisition of Olink in July 2024 at about USD 3.1bn, net of acquired cash
markets: Pharmaceutical companies, biobanks and academic researchers worldwide in oncology, immunology, neurology and cardiometabolic research.
rationale: Scientific B2B brand selling to researchers; F1 has little direct pull, though data-and-precision storytelling could support awareness among pharma clients.
parent_stake: about 98.2% tendered, remainder by compulsory redemption

name: e& PPF Telecom
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Telecom group owning Yettel in Bulgaria, Hungary and Serbia, O2 Slovakia and CETIN infrastructure, serving over 10 million customers.
ownership: subsidiary of e& (Emirates Telecommunications Group), 50% plus one share; PPF Group holds the rest
capacity_detail: e& completed purchase of a controlling stake on 24 Oct 2024 for EUR 2.15bn plus EUR 200M adjustment; combined revenue about EUR 2.0bn in 2023
markets: Mobile, broadband and infrastructure services in Bulgaria, Hungary, Serbia and Slovakia.
rationale: Yettel is a consumer mobile brand in four markets including Hungary, home of the Hungarian Grand Prix, where F1 activation could lift awareness.

name: Inari Medical
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Medical device maker of mechanical thrombectomy systems, such as FlowTriever and ClotTriever, for removing blood clots in veins.
capacity_detail: Stryker completed its acquisition of Inari on 19 February 2025 for about USD 4.9bn (USD 80 per share)
markets: Hospitals and interventional physicians in the United States and Europe (subsidiary in Basel) treating pulmonary embolism and DVT.
rationale: Specialist device brand selling to hospitals; F1 offers little direct customer reach, though clinician hospitality is conceivable.

name: Hang Seng Bank
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Major Hong Kong retail and commercial bank, a member of HSBC Group, privatised and delisted in January 2026.
ownership: subsidiary of HSBC (HSBC bought out the 38% minority it did not own)
capacity_detail: HSBC's privatisation of Hang Seng Bank (cited by Reuters as a USD 13.6bn deal for the 38% minority) was court-approved Jan 2026; operating income HKD 36.8bn in 2024
markets: Retail, wealth and commercial banking customers in Hong Kong, with operations in mainland China.
rationale: Leading Hong Kong consumer bank brand serving affluent clients; F1's strong Asian audience and Shanghai Grand Prix could support wealth-management marketing.

name: Domain
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Australian property marketplace running domain.com.au, allhomes.com.au, commercialrealestate.com.au and Pricefinder for buyers, renters and agents.
capacity_detail: CoStar agreed in May 2025 to buy 100% of Domain for AUD 3bn (Reuters: USD 1.9bn) and completed the purchase on 27 August 2025
markets: Australian residential and commercial property buyers, renters, sellers, agents and advertisers.
rationale: Consumer property portal fighting REA for Australian audience share; Melbourne Grand Prix activation could raise brand reach among affluent buyers.

name: CSR
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Australian building products maker whose brands include Gyprock, Bradford, Hebel, Cemintel, Monier and PGH bricks.
capacity_detail: Saint-Gobain acquired CSR for AUD 4.5bn (USD 2.95bn) in 2024
markets: Builders, contractors and homeowners in Australia and New Zealand buying plasterboard, insulation, bricks and roofing.
rationale: Trade-facing building materials brands with Australian reach; Melbourne race hospitality could serve builder customers, though consumer pull is modest.

name: SRS Distribution
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: US distributor of roofing, siding, solar and other building products to contractors through more than 430 branches.
capacity_detail: Home Depot agreed on 28 March 2024 to acquire SRS for USD 18.25bn; SRS is listed as a Home Depot subsidiary
markets: Professional roofing, landscaping and pool contractors across the United States.
rationale: Contractor-facing distribution brand; US Grands Prix hospitality could reward big trade customers, but consumer brand value is limited.

name: GMS
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Distributor of drywall, steel framing, insulation, ceilings and tools to contractors from over 300 locations in North America.
ownership: subsidiary of The Home Depot (via SRS)
capacity_detail: Home Depot agreed in June 2025 to buy GMS for about USD 4.3bn; completed September 2025
markets: Residential and commercial contractors in the United States and Canada.
rationale: Trade distributor selling to contractors; F1 hospitality could support key-account relationships, though the brand has little consumer pull.

name: Foundation Building Materials
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: North American distributor of wallboard, ceilings, metal framing, insulation and related interior building products to professional contractors.
capacity_detail: Lowe's agreed in August 2025 to acquire FBM for USD 8.8bn in cash; FBM is listed among Lowe's subsidiaries
markets: Professional builders and contractors in the United States and Canada.
rationale: Contractor-focused brand Lowe's uses to win pro customers; race-weekend hospitality could support trade relationships more than consumer awareness.

name: FläktGroup
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: German maker of ventilation, air handling and indoor climate systems, including Woods Air Movement, SEMCO and SE-Elektronic.
ownership: subsidiary of Samsung Electronics (bought from Triton)
capacity_detail: Samsung Electronics completed its EUR 1.5bn acquisition of FläktGroup on 6 November 2025; annual sales over EUR 700M
markets: Commercial buildings, data centres, hospitals and industrial customers in 65 countries, from 14 production sites.
rationale: Samsung is building FläktGroup into a global HVAC brand for data centres and buildings; F1 hospitality and technical storytelling could support B2B growth.

name: HPS Investment Partners
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Alternative credit investment manager overseeing about USD 201bn across private and liquid credit strategies, now part of BlackRock.
capacity_detail: BlackRock agreed in December 2024 to buy HPS for USD 12bn and completed the acquisition in July 2025
markets: Institutional investors, insurers, pension funds and wealth clients worldwide seeking private and liquid credit exposure.
rationale: Private-credit brand courting institutions and wealthy investors; F1 hospitality is a proven client-entertainment tool for asset managers.

name: Bridge Investment Group
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: US real estate investment manager with about USD 50bn of assets, kept as its own brand within Apollo.
ownership: subsidiary of Apollo Global Management (platform company within Apollo's asset management business)
capacity_detail: Apollo completed its all-stock acquisition of Bridge at an equity value of about USD 1.5bn on 2 September 2025
markets: Institutional and private-wealth investors in US residential, industrial and other real estate strategies.
rationale: Real estate fund manager raising money from wealthy investors; F1 hospitality could aid capital formation, though brand-led marketing is minimal.

name: Retina Consultants of America
group: Subsidiaries: finance, health, industrial and energy companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: US network of retina specialist practices with clinics in 23 states, majority-owned by drug distributor Cencora.
capacity_detail: Cencora completed the purchase of an 85% stake in RCA for about USD 4.4bn on 2 January 2025
markets: Patients with retinal disease across 23 US states, served through about 32 affiliated practices.
rationale: Physician practice network with local brands; F1 sponsorship offers little patient reach and is a poor commercial fit.
